artboards.title: R2 · 2 HEAT — state in the paint

annotations.text:
ROUND 3 — REFINED (the build spec)

Language: SIGNAL, picked 2026-08-30. Structure: the fused pick. The unchosen directions stay on page-2 — the record of why.

New beyond the R2 board:
· Inline capture on the fold stats — tap WATER / WEIGHT / BLOOD and the control appears in place, floating above the nav. The chips really log; values update. (Revealed-on-intent as fork 2’s answer — implied by picking the T2 fold stats. Veto if wrong.)
· post-donation scenario on the switch: eligibility window + the suppressed-endurance note, both PLACEHOLDER.
· T3 label on the nav — every component now carries its tier.
· A Hold day keeps the orange verdict: the accent means urgency, not mood — deliberate.

THE TEST (five-second, #2): on first paint, no tapping — five seconds per board. Name (1) the under-stimulated muscles, (2) the untouched adaptations, (3) push or hold. Left = good day, right = bad day. Write the answer down.

After it passes: docs/design-system.md (step 6), /ground (step 7), then code (step 8).

ROUND 2 — LOOK

Four visual directions on the picked structure. Same data, same logic, same layout on all three — only the language changes. Each is named by its axis:

1 · SIGNAL — what colour is allowed to mean. Monochrome paper; one orange accent only where action lives.

2 · HEAT — where the state lives. A single sequential teal ramp IS the read; chrome recedes.

3 · NIGHT — figure-ground. Dark dashboard, work glows, the gap is a void. Note: this inverts the ink-polarity you just chose.

4 · WASHI — identity. Peter’s palette (2026-08-29): rice paper, sumi-ink ramp, a vermillion seal, serif numerals. Three channels, one meaning each — ink = stimulus, vermillion = act on this, teal = systemic readiness.

Standing rules, honoured by all three: colour on the map = stimulus only; recovery keeps its own channel (the hatch); systemic readiness never colours the map (P5); every direction is colourblind-safe by construction (one accent / one hue / luminance only / red and teal never sharing an element).

Pick one — or name the hybrid (“2’s map with 1’s accent” is a legal answer here, unlike in round 1). Round 3 refines the winner into the build spec.

PICKED (2026-08-30): SIGNAL — refined on page-3.

THE PICK (2026-08-29) — the fused structure

Peter kept: A’s verdict header + readiness gate, the body map, B’s one-state-each whole-body strip, and the T2 fold stats.

WHAT IS MISSING did not survive as a section. The concept lands as RANKED CALLOUTS drawn on the map (direction B of the three explored): numbered labels point at the worst regions, worst first — 1 CORE (never), 2 QUADS, 3 GLUTES, 4 HAMS, with CALVES unnumbered below the act-on-these cut. The verdict names the top gap as its reason line. POWER (muscle-linked, 0 sets everywhere) is a footnote under the map — on the muscle side, not in the cardio strip (P2).

Held state: the callouts never change — the gate changes the instruction, never the facts. Compare the two boards above.

This implies both §6 answers (readiness GATES; whole-body ONE STATE EACH) — to be recorded in roadmap 010 once confirmed. Round 2 proper (visual directions) builds on this board.

POLARITY FLIPPED (same day, Peter’s call): ink = training accumulated, light/empty = the gap — heatmap convention; the numbered callouts carry the gap-salience now. The round-1 boards below keep the old darker-is-gap mapping as the record of the fork.

ROUND 1 — STRUCTURE

Grey boxes, real numbers, one type weight. No colour or type decisions yet — those are round 2.

The five-second test needs NO tapping and NO switches: row 1 is a good day, row 2 is the same two screens on a bad day.

Look at each for five seconds. Can you name (1) which muscles are under-stimulated, (2) which adaptations are untouched, (3) whether to push today?

Write the answer down. Then start tapping.

FORK 1 — where readiness sits

A: readiness GATES THE INSTRUCTION. The screen fuses both signals into one verdict — on a bad day it says Hold, the readiness card takes the emphasis, and every gap flips from “train this” (solid) to “held” (hollow). Nothing is hidden or dimmed: the gate changes the instruction, never the facts.

B: readiness sits ALONGSIDE. Two facts, equal weight, and you combine them yourself. The screen never issues a verdict.

Second question, answered differently in each: the three whole-body qualities — all cardio, after the 2026-08-29 simplification — get ONE combined read in A, ONE STATE EACH in B.

THE HELD STATE (row 2, screen A)

An earlier draft dimmed the whole local read to 34% and struck through the gap chips. That read as “broken / no data”, not “don’t push” — and it violated the map’s own rule that darker = bigger gap.

The redesign: recovery gates the ACTION, never the FACT. The map keeps full contrast, the legend stays crisp, and a chip is never crossed out — it goes hollow, with a HELD tag, because the gap is still true.

Compare with B beside it: B changes nothing at all on a bad day. That is the fork.

THE TIERS

T1 — on screen the moment Home paints. This is the entire five-second answer and nothing else. Ships in the initial chunk.

T2 — appears when the read raises a question: a drill-in, a detail, an inline capture. Lazy chunk, prefetched on hover.

T3 — reached by an explicit destination change. Lazy chunk, no prefetch.

If the glance needs a tap, T1 is wrong. If every chart is in T1, the bundle is wrong.

LOGGING GOES THROUGH AN EXERCISE

“Log sets for Quads” cannot just add a count: sets classify into adaptations BY REP RANGE, so a bare +3 would write sets no read can use. (The earlier +1/+3/+5 idea is dead for this reason.)

So the button opens a ranked list of the exercises that already feed this muscle — most recent first, one tap repeats the last scheme — then a prefilled sets grid. “Something else” hands off to the full exercise list (T3).

Exercise names are real; the rep/load schemes are SAMPLE values (per-set history wasn’t in the step-0 pull).

Tap through it on the left artboard; the right one shows the flow already open.

FORK 2 — when the capture control exists

The same fork three times: always-visible quick-add (T1) vs revealed-on-intent (T2). Both work on all three artboards — tap them.

Water is logged daily. Donation three times a year. Body weight twice a month. One answer has to cover all three, and it decides three folds at once.

THE MODEL, SIMPLIFIED (2026-08-29)

Nine adaptations became seven.

· SPEED — dropped. Pure speed isn’t trained here.
· SKILL — dropped for now. Too broad for an app to track honestly; maybe per-exercise recommendations later.
· POWER — reclassified: force × velocity of a specific muscle group, so it reads PER MUSCLE (drill-in quality mix), not whole-body.

What’s left splits cleanly: four muscle-linked qualities (strength, hypertrophy, muscular endurance, power) on the map and drill-in; three whole-body ones (VO₂max, anaerobic, endurance) — all cardio — in the strip.

App-side execution: roadmap 019.

PLACEHOLDERS

Every physiological threshold on this canvas is marked PLACEHOLDER and is NOT decided:

· 60 sets per muscle per cycle
· recovered after 48 h
· 3.0 L hydration target
· donation windows 14 / 56 days
· the readiness push threshold

/ground runs before any of these becomes code.

Rep/load schemes in the log flow are sample values, not history.
